summary.headline: GK Energy H1 FY27 revenue rose 38.9% to INR 907.8 crore, with Q2 revenue up 12.3% to INR 402.7 crore and receivables still stretched at 204 days.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 38.9% to INR 907.8 crore, EBITDA rose 21.6% to INR 160.5 crore at a 17.7% margin, and PAT grew 30.7% to INR 109 crore. Q2, seasonally the weakest quarter, saw revenue up 12.3% to INR 402.7 crore, EBITDA of INR 74.4 crore (18.5% margin) and PAT of INR 49.4 crore. Management highlighted INR 377.5 crore of customer collections since 30 September, which cut receivable days from 204 to about 128 on its calculation. The company is widening from solar pumps into rooftop solar and its first utility-scale BESS order (150 MW / 300 MWh).

financial_highlights.change: about 128 days after INR 377.5 crore collected since 30 Sep

segments.name: Solar pumps (agriculture)
segments.commentary: Q2 installations of 19,391 systems (up 41.8% YoY) and 84 MW commissioned (up 33.3%). H1 installations 43,509 (up 77.6%) and 193 MW commissioned (up 70.8%). Additional institutional order of 14,000 off-grid pumps in Maharashtra received October 2026.

segments.name: Retail and institutional rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Management says retail rooftop is growing strongly; more than 2,000 systems installed and 4,000-5,000 system demand cited. Institutional order to install one lakh rooftop systems; an order of around INR 450 crore was referenced on the call.

segments.name: BESS (battery storage, utility-scale)
segments.commentary: First order for 150 MW / 300 MWh utility-scale installation. Company plans to build its own BESS plants and sell power to DISCOMs under a fixed-revenue model for 15 years; intends to expand to 2 GW in the midterm.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin to be maintained at 17-18%, per management's reaffirmation on the call.
Two-digit PAT margin targeted for FY27.
FY27 growth of about 40% expected even without PM KUSUM; with PM KUSUM management said it is on track for INR 3,000 crore top line.
PM KUSUM 2.0 expected to be announced in Q3 FY27, with benefits from Q4 FY27 onwards, per management.
Year-end FY27 receivable days guided at 120-150 days.
Rooftop margins expected slightly below pump margins; rooftop working capital cycle 45-60 days.
Long-term ambition: 1 million installed systems and USD 1 billion business by 2030.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: manufacturing outsourced to partners across 8 states; no owned factories.
Module/cell supply: confirmatory agreement with module-cell makers for 875 MW this year; about 300 MW bought from two cell makers last year.
BESS capex broadly INR 90 lakh to INR 1 crore per MWh (management's broad estimate); battery cycle life 8,000-10,000 cycles currently.
Cumulative base above 1,84,000 systems and over 800 MW across India; network of six states, 7,500+ villages, 20,000+ warehouses, 40+ owned vehicles, 1,300+ installation partners.
demand_pricing: Order book stands at INR 788 crore, covering orders as of 30 September 2026 plus orders received from 1 October 2026.
Cumulative FY27 orders of INR 1,422.29 crore incl. GST, excluding the BESS order. Management said close to INR 900 crore of the order book has already been executed.
Management said it needs about INR 500 crore of fresh orders to reach its INR 2,200 crore revenue scenario without PM KUSUM.
Pump receivables described as a pan-India average tied to government scheme payments after survey, installation, inspection; farmers pay their share upfront.
Rooftop is cash-and-carry per management, with margins targeted slightly below pumps.

qa_highlights.question: Management referenced INR 1,800 crore order visibility in a media interview versus INR 788 crore order book in the presentation: which is right?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 1,800 crore is revenue visibility covering the current year's order book plus opening order book; close to INR 900 crore has already been executed.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 margins hold at 17-18% given Q1 about 16% and Q2 about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it intends to maintain the 17-18% range, citing planning and a controlled manufacturing ecosystem, and is confident it will do so.

qa_highlights.question: What drives 35-40% growth if PM KUSUM is delayed, and how does it square with the INR 788 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the existing pump orders, retail rooftop, and Magel Tyala 7 pipeline; it said about INR 500 crore of new orders must be secured to reach INR 2,200 crore total.

qa_highlights.question: Why are pump receivables so stretched at over six months, and is the model perennially long-dated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections are from government schemes after the installation and inspection cycle, the figure is pan-India, and it is guiding to 120 days, maximum 140 days; post-quarter collections cut it to about 128 days.

qa_highlights.question: What are rooftop margins and working capital needs for the large rooftop order?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected slightly lower than pumps; total cash cycle is 45-60 days in rooftop.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and reason for PM KUSUM 2.0 delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied a delay, saying it had guided to Q3 announcement and benefits from Q4 onwards; technical discussions on product upgrades are ongoing with management's input.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be fresh equity or more borrowing to fund working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no fresh equity plan at current prices; promoters at about 79% would dilute to 75% in about two years if needed; debt raised so far is considered sufficient.

risks_watch: Trade receivables of INR 1,012.38 crore at 30 September (204 days); collection of year-end 120-150 days is the key watch item.
PM KUSUM 2.0 timing: the FY27 upside case depends on a Q3 announcement and benefits starting in Q4.
FY27 revenue target of INR 3,000 crore implies a large H2 ramp; order book of INR 788 crore covers only part of it.
Dependence on module and cell supply from outsourced partners, with cell sourcing expected to ease in 1-1.5 years per management.
BESS entry involves capex-heavy own-asset model; capex and working-capital intensity not quantified by the company.
Promoter stake of about 79% versus 75% target means future equity dilution is possible within two years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on growth, margins and PM KUSUM timing, though evasive on the gap between the INR 1,800 crore and INR 788 crore order figures and on the receivables trajectory. Management repeatedly dismissed the delay question and reframed the 120-day receivable guidance against the post-quarter collection figure.
key_quotes: We are no longer a single product Company. We are becoming a renewable energy platform across generation, storage, and delivery.
So we are very confident. Yes, we will definitely going to maintain that.
GK Energy will not get any kind of the shortage for the DCR cell or the DCR model, because model is already commodity, cell is going to become a commodity in one and half year itself.
Year-end, we are expecting 120 to 150 max days would be there year-end on the receivable side.

adds.what: Owned BESS plants planned (no owned factories; manufacturing outsourced); 150 MW / 300 MWh first utility-scale BESS order, expansion to 2 GW in midterm

growth.why: Management guides close to 40% FY27 revenue growth even without PM KUSUM (INR 3,000 crore if PM KUSUM on track), backed by an INR 788 crore order book, INR 1,422 crore cumulative FY27 orders, and a 14,000-pump Maharashtra order; capacity is asset-light with outsourced manufacturing and no owned capacity additions, so the backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management intends to hold 17-18% EBITDA margin (Q1 about 16%, Q2 18.5%); rooftop margins guided slightly below pumps, so mix dilutes margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Asset-light model with manufacturing outsourced across 8 states and no owned factories; owned BESS plants are planned but no timing or capex is quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pump installations up 77.6% in H1 to 43,509 systems and 14,000-pump Maharashtra order received Oct 2026; FY27 growth of ~40% guided even without PM KUSUM.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure given and capex is not discussed for pumps; BESS owned-plant build (INR 90 lakh-1 crore per MWh, 2 GW midterm ambition) could bring a capex announcement, but no date or approval was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed close to 40% growth and 17-18% EBITDA margin rather than raising; H1 revenue grew 38.9% but Q2 grew only 12.3%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 INR 3,000 crore top line needs a large H2 ramp and PM KUSUM 2.0 is guided for Q3 announcement; INR 788 crore order book covers only part of it, and year-end receivables of 120-150 days are a watch item at 204 days on 30 Sep.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rooftop solar scaling (institutional order for one lakh systems, ~INR 450 crore referenced) and first 150 MW / 300 MWh utility BESS order are underway; PM KUSUM 2.0 benefits guided from Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Need ~INR 500 crore fresh orders for INR 2,200 crore scenario
rows.why: Order book is INR 788 crore with close to INR 900 crore already executed; management says about INR 500 crore of new orders is needed for the INR 2,200 crore scenario without PM KUSUM, and cumulative FY27 orders are INR 1,422.29 crore excl. BESS.

rows.label: Receivable days down to 120-150 by year-end FY27
rows.why: Receivables were INR 1,012.38 crore at 204 days on 30 Sep, and INR 377.5 crore collected since then cut them to about 128 days on management's calculation; guidance is 120-150 days at year-end.

rows.label: Equity dilution if promoter stake falls toward 75%
rows.why: Promoters hold about 79%; management says no fresh equity at current prices but would dilute to about 75% in about two years if needed, with debt raised so far considered sufficient.

tone.note: Management was confident on 40% FY27 growth, 17-18% EBITDA margin and PM KUSUM timing, but was evasive on the INR 1,800 crore vs INR 788 crore order gap and on receivables, while analysts pressed on the PM KUSUM delay and the receivable trajectory.
